Definition: destructive, i.e. (as noun) destruction, literally (specifically a snare) or figuratively (corruption)
BiblicalUsage: mashchîyth is destruction and corruption, the destroyer at work. In 2 Chronicles 20:23 Ammon and Moab stand up to destroy the inhabitants of Seir, and then help to destroy one another. In Daniel 10:8 Daniel's comeliness is turned into corruption and he retains no strength, and in 2 Kings 23:13 the mount of corruption is defiled by Josiah. In 2 Chronicles 22:4 the counsellors of Ahaziah are his destruction, and the word is the ruin that works from within.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mashchîyth shows me that corruption works quietly, turning strength to nothing. I hold that God alone can keep me from the destroyer.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
